newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says Kennecott cost US$150 mln in 96.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says Kennecott cost US$150 mln in 96.

text.p: Anglo-Australian mining and smelting group RTZ-CRA said on Thursday that problems at its Kennecott copper smelter in the United States cost the group about US$150 million in lost earnings in 1996.

"If we (had) operated 100 percent design capacity through last year, our net earnings would have been about US$150 million higher," Robert Wilson, executive chairman of RTZ-CRA, told a video news conference from London.

Refined copper production from Bingham Canyon, Utah, where the Kennecott smelter is located, was 24 percent lower than expectations in 1996 due to the slower than anticipated buildup of throughput at the new smelter, RTZ-CRA said.
The design capacity for the smelter is 270,000 tonnes of copper a year.
The smelter's flash converting furnace is scheduled to be shut down for about six weeks in the second quarter of 1997 to replace refractories and install new cooling blocks.
Improvements will also be made in the smelter's anode casting facility at the same time, the company said.
RTZ-CRA earlier reported a calendar 1996 net profit of US$1.096 billion, down from $1.441 billion in 1995.
